title.value: Towards Better Evaluation for Dynamic Link Prediction
title.justification: The title captures the essence of the paper, which is about improving evaluation methodologies for dynamic link prediction in graphs.
title.quote: Towards Better Evaluation for Dynamic Link Prediction

extractions.description: The paper discusses challenges and proposes new evaluation methods for dynamic link prediction in graphs, emphasizing the importance of more robust negative sampling strategies and diverse datasets. It introduces a memorization-based baseline called EdgeBank and offers new datasets from underrepresented domains to provide better evaluation scenarios for dynamic learning methods.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: While the paper discusses methodologies and challenges in dynamic link prediction, it does not directly address climate or ecological sustainability.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Despite the prevalence of recent success in learning from static graphs, learning from time-evolving graphs remains an open challenge. In this work, we design new, more stringent evaluation procedures for link prediction specific to dynamic graphs, which reflect real-world considerations, to better compare the strengths and weaknesses of methods.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not directly relate to climate or ecological sustainable development. It focuses on improving methods for evaluating dynamic link prediction in graphs, which does not tie into the predefined categories for sustainable development.
primary_category.quote: The goal of this work is to propose more effective evaluation strategies to better differentiate dynamic link prediction methods.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper's focus on evaluation strategies and dynamic link prediction is not relevant to any secondary Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development category.
secondary_categories.quote: Existing benchmark datasets are mostly social or interaction networks thus limited in domain diversity.

primary_sub_category.quote: We propose a pure memorization-based baseline, named EdgeBank, which simply stores previously observed edges in memory, and then predicts existing edges in memory as positive at test time.

secondary_sub_categories.quote: To facilitate more efficient learning on dynamic graphs, many efforts have been devoted to the development of dynamic graph representation learning methods.
